comment: Cross-language behavioral contract for the session-events artifact (`events/<name>.ndjson`).
This file is the single source of truth for the two rules both implementations must agree on:
(1) fileNames — how a file name maps to a stream name (including the legacy `.json` style-segment
strip), implemented by Kotlin `SessionEvents.parseFileName` and TS `parseStreamFileName`;
(2) lines — how one NDJSON line decodes to an ordering timestamp + payload (the `{timeMs, data}`
envelope rule), implemented by the Kotlin `SessionEventsReader` and TS `decodeEventLine`;
(3) attachments — which embedded objects a decoded payload's sweep reports as attachment refs
(the `"$attachment": true` exact-dispatch contract), implemented by Kotlin
`AttachmentRef.findAll` and TS `findAttachmentRefs`;
(4) safePaths — which attachment paths stay inside the session directory, implemented by TS
`isSafeSessionRelativePath` and the CI uploader's `_is_safe_session_relative`. Those two must
accept the SAME set: the report links every path it accepts, so a path the uploader alone
rejects ships a green build whose link 404s.
Consumed by SessionEventsParityFixturesTest (Kotlin), run-report-events.test.ts (TS) and
test_session_attachment_artifacts.py (the CI uploader). Kotlin reads only the sections it
implements.
In `lines`, `payload: null` means the line is skipped entirely; `t: null` means the line carries
no ordering timestamp (the JVM reader represents that as 0). In `attachments`, `refs` is the
exact expected sweep result in document order, `label: null` meaning absent. ACCEPTED `sizeBytes`
values here stay inside the range BOTH languages represent exactly (|n| < 2^53): above it JS has
already rounded in `JSON.parse` before either rule runs, which is a property of the wire in JS
and not a difference in the contract, so it is not something a shared fixture can pin. A size at
or past 2^63 IS pinned, as a rejection: both languages refuse it rather than clamp, because it
cannot be the contract's Long. To change
any rule: update both implementations AND this fixture in the same change — never one
language's tests alone.

value.text: two refs, nested at different depths, reported in document order

safePaths.why: a leading tilde is an ordinary file-name character; nothing on either path expands it
dots only matter as a WHOLE segment
